title: Fragment soaking of crystals by Echo acoustic dispensing
summary: Fragments in DMSO (100 mM) are shot from a source plate straight into crystallisation drops with an Echo, aimed away from the crystals so the solvent diffuses in gently. Soak 4-6 h or overnight, then harvest. This is the core XChem soaking method.

steps.text: Prepare fragment source plate (1536-well Echo format) at 100 mM in DMSO.
Choose the DMSO load: crystals tolerated around 20% when hit directly and up to about 40% when the solvent is aimed away; across 16 targets the optimum was 10-40% (mean about 23%).
Unseal the crystal plate (SwissCI 3-drop sitting-drop plate) and mount it inverted above the source plate; unsealing takes 1-2 minutes per plate.
Transfer 5-50 nL per drop in 2.5 nL droplets at 200 Hz, targeting the drop edge away from the crystal; solvent diffuses in over 2-5 minutes.

duration_s.note: Diffusion over 2-5 min; ~1000 transfers can be done in under 10 minutes.

steps.text: Reseal the plate and let crystals soak: 4-6 h for routine screening, overnight for weak binders; strong binders may appear within minutes.
Hand the plate on for harvesting and cryo-cooling.

materials: Fragment library in DMSO, 1536-well Echo source plate
safety: DMSO penetrates skin and carries solutes with it; wear gloves.
Unseal plates only briefly to limit evaporation.

source.publisher: Acta Crystallographica Section D (IUCr, via PMC)

notes: Paper used Echo 550; catalog id beckman_echo_525 (the catalog entry that includes crystal_soaking) is the nearest match. Citation is Collins et al., 'Gentle, fast and effective crystal soaking by acoustic dispensing'.
